item.title: Autoridades de la Fed enfrían las expectativas de una subida de tasas en octubre
item.description: Dos de los principales responsables de la política monetaria de la Reserva Federal defendieron la necesidad de recabar más datos antes de decidir los próximos pasos, lo que llevó a algunos agentes de los mercados financieros a descartar un alza de tasas de interés en la reunión prevista en octubre,
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Dos de los principales responsables de la política monetaria de la Reserva Federal defendieron la necesidad de recabar más datos antes de decidir los próximos pasos, lo que llevó a algunos agentes de los mercados financieros a descartar un alza de tasas de interés en la reunión prevista en octubre, "No hay necesidad de urgencia" de modificar la configuración actual de la política monetaria, dijo el martes John Williams, presidente de la Reserva Federal de Nueva York, durante una intervención en la Universidad de Buffalo. Williams también ocupa el cargo de vicepresidente del Comité Federal de Mercado Abierto, el órgano del banco central encargado de fijar las tasas de interés. El vicepresidente de la Reserva Federal, Philip Jefferson, se hizo eco de esa opinión el jueves. "Cualquier ajuste futuro de la política monetaria debe determinarse tras examinar cuidadosamente las tendencias de los datos, la evolución de las perspectivas y el equilibrio de riesgos", dijo el número dos del banco en el texto de su intervención en la Darden School of Business de la Universidad de Virginia. Tras señalar que los mercados están "reevaluando" las perspectivas en un contexto de subida de los rendimientos del mercado de bonos, Jefferson dijo: "Mis colegas y yo tendremos que formarnos nuestra propia opinión, lo que puede llevar más tiempo". "Con más datos disponibles, estas tendencias pueden permitir un mejor análisis, al igual que la postura adecuada de la política monetaria", agregó. Los comentarios de Williams fueron un acontecimiento clave para los mercados y contribuyeron a disipar las expectativas de que la Fed subiría el costo del crédito en la reunión del Comité Federal de Mercado Abierto (FOMC, por sus siglas en inglés) del 27 al 28 de octubre. Los comentarios de Jefferson contribuyeron a consolidar el cambio de perspectiva. Las corredurías esperan ahora, en su mayoría, que la Fed suba las tasas solo una vez más este año, en diciembre en lugar de en octubre. ORIENTACIONES "INUSUALMENTE CLARAS" Jefferson "ha confirmado el mensaje del presidente de la Fed de Nueva York, Williams: la Fed no prevé aplicar una subida de tasas consecutiva en su próxima reunión de octubre y se tomará más tiempo para evaluar la evolución de las condiciones económicas", dijeron analistas de Evercore ISI. "Creemos que el mensaje conjunto de Jefferson y Williams tiene peso" en un contexto en el que el presidente de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, no está proporcionando mucha orientación, si es que ofrece alguna, sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés. Tim Duy, economista jefe para EEUU de SGH Macro, señaló que "creemos que Williams tenía que ser inusualmente claro porque las expectativas del mercado respecto a las subidas de tasas se estaban desmarcando de la Fed. Esto es consecuencia de la falta de orientación prospectiva" por parte del presidente de la Fed, explicó Duy a sus clientes. Los dos responsables monetarios se pronunciaron después de que la institución elevó su objetivo de tasas de interés un cuarto de punto porcentual en su reunión de política monetaria de mediados de septiembre, al rango de entre 3,75% y 4%. Las previsiones oficiales también apuntaban a una nueva subida este año. Otros responsables de la Fed también están de acuerdo en esperar un tiempo antes de modificar el costo del crédito, incluido uno a quien le preocupa que la política actual de tasas de interés no esté frenando la economía en gran medida, si es que lo hace. "Tengo una mente abierta" respecto a cómo procederá la Fed con las subidas de tasas y "no tengo una opinión firme" sobre si la próxima subida debería darse a finales de mes, dijo el jueves a Reuters el presidente de la Fed de Mineápolis, Neel Kashkari, en una entrevista.

item.title: Ações se recuperam e fecham em alta, conforme rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro recuam
item.description: As ações nos EUA se recuperaram das perdas iniciais e fecharam em alta nesta quinta-feira, com o S&P 500 se recuperando de uma mínima de duas semanas, à medida que a onda de vendas de títulos globais inverteu o curso após levar os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA a máximas de várias décadas.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Johann Cherian
item.content:encoded: As ações nos EUA se recuperaram das perdas iniciais e fecharam em alta nesta quinta-feira, com o S&P 500 se recuperando de uma mínima de duas semanas, à medida que a onda de vendas de títulos globais inverteu o curso após levar os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA a máximas de várias décadas. As ações ficaram sob pressão no início do pregão, já que os dados econômicos continuavam indicando uma economia sólida com pressões persistentes sobre os preços, o que alimentou temores de que a inflação pudesse, em última instância, forçar o Federal Reserve a adotar uma postura mais agressiva nas altas das taxas de juros. O Departamento do Trabalho informou que os pedidos semanais de auxílio-desemprego caíram para 197.000, abaixo da previsão de 200.000 feita por economistas consultados pela Reuters. Esse foi o mais recente de uma série de relatórios divulgados nesta semana que indicaram que o mercado de trabalho está em boa forma, antes do relatório oficial de empregos do governo, a ser divulgado na sexta-feira. Os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro ampliaram os ganhos, e a taxa de referência do título de 10 anos atingiu o nível mais alto em 24 anos, após encerrar setembro com seu maior ganho trimestral desde 1994, o que pressionou as ações para baixo depois que o Instituto de Gestão de Suprimentos (ISM) informou que seu Índice de Gerentes de Compras (PMI) do setor manufatureiro recuou para 54,5 no mês passado, ante 54,6 em agosto, e mostrou um salto nos preços dos insumos, aumentando as preocupações com a inflação. RENDIMENTOS DOS TÍTULOS DO TESOURO INVERTEM TENDÊNCIA Mas os rendimentos começaram a cair com a entrada de compradores e recuaram ainda mais depois que o vice-chair do Fed Philip Jefferson sugeriu que o banco central pode ser paciente antes de aumentar as taxas novamente, após um aumento de 25 pontos-base em setembro. O rendimento do título do Tesouro dos EUA de dois anos , que normalmente acompanha as expectativas de taxas de juros do Fed, caiu cerca de 10 pontos-base e estava prestes a registrar sua maior queda diária desde agosto de 2025. “Embora as avaliações tenham caído, o mercado ainda não está barato, então não estou pessimista em relação ao mercado de ações. Podemos seguir em frente, mas espero maior volatilidade tanto nas ações quanto nos títulos”, disse Scott Welch, diretor de investimentos da Certuity em Potomac, Maryland. “Todo mundo está se adaptando a um novo normal. Não há nada particularmente assustador no que está acontecendo nos mercados neste momento; é apenas um pouco diferente do que as pessoas estavam acostumadas a lidar nos últimos anos, e vai exigir alguma adaptação.” O Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) teve variação positiva de 0,04%, para 50.926,74 pontos, o S&P 500 (.SPX) subiu 0,20%, para 7.666,48 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) oscilou 0,04% para cima, a 26.871,60 pontos. SETOR DE ENERGIA LIDERA GANHOS Os preços do petróleo também continuaram alimentando os temores de inflação. O petróleo Brent fechou com alta de mais de US$4 por barril depois que a China suspendeu as exportações de combustível, ameaçando restringir ainda mais os mercados. O salto nos preços do petróleo ajudou a impulsionar o índice de energia do S&P 500 (.SPNY) 1,9%, tornando-o o setor com melhor desempenho entre os 11 principais setores do S&P. O setor de tecnologia (.SPLRCT) também mostrou alguma força, com alta de 0,8%, enquanto as ações de software (.SPLRCIS) subiram 1% com os resultados da Accenture (ACN.N) . As ações da empresa de consultoria em TI avançaram, fechando no nível mais alto desde 6 de março, após a empresa prever um crescimento da receita anual acima das estimativas. A Micron Technology (MU.O) fechou com alta de 3%, já que uma previsão de receita melhor do que o esperado e US$32 bilhões em compromissos com clientes sob seus contratos de fornecimento reforçaram a confiança no setor de IA. Dados de inflação mais fracos do que o esperado, divulgados na quarta-feira, enfraqueceram ainda mais as expectativas de que o Fed aumentasse as taxas em sua reunião de outubro. Os mercados agora precificam apenas 28,2% de chance de um aumento de pelo menos 25 pontos-base, ante 68,6% na semana anterior, de acordo com o CME FedWatch. Após os comentários de Jefferson, o presidente do Federal Reserve de Minneapolis, Neel Kashkari, disse que espera que sejam necessários aumentos adicionais nas taxas para conter a economia rumo a 2027, embora não tenha certeza se o próximo movimento deva ocorrer neste mês.

item.title: Wall Street regulator proposes rules on investment adviser crypto asset custody
item.description: The US Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday proposed new rules it said would help govern investment funds' custody of crypto assets under federal securities laws, according to a statement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday proposed new rules it said would help govern investment funds' custody of crypto assets under federal securities laws, according to a statement. SEC Chair Paul Atkins said in a statement the new regulations "would provide a clear regulatory framework for the custody of crypto assets, giving investment advisers and funds a compliant pathway where none existed before."

item.title: Nike plans more job cuts to boost sputtering turnaround, forecasts steep revenue drop
item.description: Nike is deepening its restructuring under CEO Elliott Hill as its woes in China intensify, announcing a plan to cut more jobs and shake up its global business divisions after the sportswear giant projected a surprisingly steep drop in full-year revenue.
item.dc:creator: Danielle Kaye, Angela M
item.content:encoded: Nike (NKE.N) is deepening its restructuring under CEO Elliott Hill as its woes in China intensify, announcing a plan to cut more jobs and shake up its global business divisions after the sportswear giant projected a surprisingly steep drop in full-year revenue. The tepid forecast on Thursday underscored that Nike's challenges will likely persist for at least several more quarters — especially in China, where sales tumbled 26% on a constant-currency basis in the first quarter — adding to investor unease about the pace of Hill's turnaround. Its shares fell 8.5% in extended trading. The company has been working to revive growth during the first two years of Hill's tenure by refocusing on key sports such as running and by rebuilding relationships with wholesale retailers. But analysts say its worries have in large part stemmed from a failure to release enough new, compelling products, leading to an uptick in promotions and discounts. "Our Nike performance business is not yet large enough to offset the pressure we're seeing in Nike sportswear, Jordan brand, and Greater China," Hill said on a post-earnings call. Reviving those weak areas of Nike's business "will take time," he said, pointing to a deliberate reduction in the volume of Jordan retro launches. The company, which also missed analysts' expectations for first-quarter revenue, unveiled changes to its operating model, including job cuts and a move to three geographic regions — Americas, Asia Pacific and Greater China, and EMEA — instead of four. It plans to open a new campus in India "with strong capabilities and access to talent." Nike said the company does not yet know the number of roles that will be cut under the restructuring. It will begin notifying employees in 2027. The program, building on [USN:L6N4161GI TEXT:"previous rounds of layoffs"], including one announced earlier this year, is expected to deliver about $2.5 billion in savings through fiscal 2031, with the majority set to be realized in fiscal years 2029 and 2030. Nike expects its revenue to decline in the high single digit in fiscal 2027. Analysts, on average, estimate full-year revenue to drop about 2%, according to data compiled by LSEG. "There is nothing inherently wrong with the (restructuring) plans, but they do suggest that Nike's current model is not really fit for purpose, which in turn raises the question of why these changes were not made sooner," said Neil Saunders, managing director of GlobalData. CHINA SALES PLUMMET, AGAIN China, historically a profit-driver for Nike, has shown particular weakness in recent quarters as international rivals and domestic sportswear groups gain traction. Investors remain focused on any signs of improvement, which analysts say will hinge in large part on local product innovation. Sales in China have fallen for nine consecutive quarters, with the slowdown accelerating in the reported period. The region accounts for about 15% of Nike's annual revenue and is its third-largest market after North America and Europe, the Middle East and Africa. The company recently said that starting in January, it will [USN:L6N43O0N0 TEXT:"pull online sales rights"] from some of its biggest retail partners in China — a high-stakes bet that tighter control over pricing and distribution can revive its fortunes. But the digital cleanup will take "multiple seasons," Hill warned on Thursday, adding that near-term revenue and profitability in China will take a hit. Analysts have also questioned whether the abrupt measures, though likely to help Nike address rampant discounting, will convince Chinese consumers that they want what Nike is selling. "Nike does not have a channel problem in China, but rather a product problem," BNP Paribas senior analyst Laurent Vasilescu has said in a research note, adding that he was surprised by the company's short timeframe to shut down online wholesale in China. Sales in North America, Nike's biggest region, rose 2% on a constant-currency basis, in one sign of relative strength in the first quarter. Nike's performance business, specifically, contributed to the growth, benefiting from the World Cup, Hill said. Adding to the company's challenges, French soccer star [USN:L4N45A123 TEXT:"Kylian Mbappe ended a two-decade-long partnership with Nike"] in September and joined Swiss-based rival On. Nike's quarterly sales fell about 4% to $11.21 billion in the first quarter, compared with analysts' average estimate of $11.32 billion. Its gross margin, however, rose 60 basis points to 42.8% in the quarter ended August 31, helped by lower warehousing and logistics costs. Hill said Nike would update its targets through the fiscal year, beginning in November, as it works through the restructuring plan. The company had withdrawn annual forecasts in October 2024 to provide then new-CEO Hill with some flexibility to assess its business. S&P Dow Jones Indices removed Nike from the S&P 100 (.OEX) in September as part of a quarterly rebalancing after 18 years in the index of blue-chip companies.

item.title: US-India trade deal not imminent, Greer says
item.description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Thursday the Trump administration was working with India to finalize a bilateral trade deal, but added an agreement was not imminent.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Thursday the Trump administration was working with India to finalize a bilateral trade deal, but added an agreement was not imminent. Greer said he had "a very constructive conversation" with Indian Trade Minister Piyush Goyal at the G20 trade ministers meeting in Milwaukee this week and that officials from the two countries were continuing the conservation. "I don't think there's something imminent, but we truly have identified the universe of items that are sticking points. We're working diligently toward them," he added.

item.title: Açúcar bruto atinge máxima em 18 meses; café arábica cai
item.description: Os contratos futuros do açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE atingiram nesta quinta-feira a maior cotação em 18 meses, impulsionados por preocupações com a safra em vários dos principais países produtores, enquanto os preços do café arábica caíram.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros do açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE atingiram nesta quinta-feira a maior cotação em 18 meses, impulsionados por preocupações com a safra em vários dos principais países produtores, enquanto os preços do café arábica caíram. AÇÚCAR * O primeiro contrato de açúcar bruto fechou em alta de 0,33 centavos, ou 1,8%, a 18,94 centavos por libra-peso, após atingir uma máxima de 18 meses de 19,05 centavos. * Operadores afirmaram que o mercado foi sustentado por preocupações de que vários produtores importantes possam registrar uma queda na produção na safra 2026/27, incluindo Índia, Tailândia e União Europeia. * Eles observaram, no entanto, que a oferta está ampla no momento. * A entrega referente ao contrato de outubro, que foi a maior de 2026, foi vista como um fator de baixa, reforçando a percepção de que o mercado está bem abastecido no momento. * O vencimento registrou entregas de 1,45 milhão de toneladas métricas, tendo a brasileira BTG Pactual Commodities como principal fornecedora e a empresa asiática Wilmar como única receptora do açúcar, segundo os corretores. * Esperava-se que parte do açúcar fosse destinada à Indonésia, onde a produção de cana-de-açúcar caiu significativamente este ano devido ao fenômeno climático El Niño. * No Brasil, a produção de açúcar caiu 41,6% na primeira quinzena de setembro, segundo o governo, à medida que as chuvas continuam a atrapalhar o trabalho no campo. * O preço do açúcar branco subiu 0,2%, para US$ 507,30 por tonelada métrica. CAFÉ * O café robusta ficou praticamente estável, a US$ 3.448 por tonelada. * Os corretores observaram que o Vietnã, maior produtor de robusta, entrou oficialmente em sua nova safra na quinta-feira, embora os operadores tenham afirmado que é improvável que os grãos recém-colhidos cheguem em grandes quantidades antes do início de novembro. * "Os preços da próxima safra ainda não foram determinados. Eles dependerão de vários fatores, incluindo a situação no Brasil e as condições climáticas no Planalto Central no próximo mês, embora as condições atuais sejam favoráveis para os cafezais", disse um trader da região. * As exportações de café robusta de Sumatra, na Indonésia, caíram 13,5% em agosto, segundo dados comerciais. * O preço do café arábica caiu 0,8%, para US$2,8825 por libra-peso. CACAU * O preço de referência do cacau em Nova York fechou em alta de US$14, ou 0,3%, para US$5.381 por tonelada, após atingir uma mínima de dois meses de US$5.051. * Os corretores afirmaram que o mercado continuou sendo pressionado pelo excesso de oferta, em decorrência de um grande superávit global na safra 2025/26 (outubro/setembro). * O cacau em Londres subiu 0,4%, para £4.032 por tonelada. (Reportagem de Nigel Hunt e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: ExxonMobil e TotalEnergies arrematam 1 mi barris cada em leilão de petróleo da União, diz PPSA
item.description: A ExxonMobil e a TotalEnergies arremataram, cada uma, 1 milhão de barris em leilão de petróleo da União, realizado pela estatal brasileira Pré-Sal Petróleo SA (PPSA), informou a empresa em comunicado nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A ExxonMobil e a TotalEnergies arremataram, cada uma, 1 milhão de barris em leilão de petróleo da União, realizado pela estatal brasileira Pré-Sal Petróleo SA (PPSA), informou a empresa em comunicado nesta quinta-feira. No leilão, a ExxonMobil venceu a carga a ser produzida no campo de Bacalhau, enquanto a TotalEnergies do campo de Búzios, disse a PPSA, que representa os direitos da União nos contratos de partilha de produção. Os carregamentos estão previstos para novembro deste ano. O 9º Leilão Spot de Petróleo da União ofertou cerca de 5 milhões de barris de petróleo do campo de Búzios e uma carga de aproximadamente 1 milhão de barris de petróleo do campo de Bacalhau. As cargas que não foram arrematadas serão ofertadas no dia 7 de outubro de 2026, segundo a PPSA. Além da ExxonMobil e da TotalEnergies, participaram do certame: CNOOC, Equinor, Galp, Petrobras, Petrochina e Prio.

item.title: Preço da soja cai em Chicago por colheita nos EUA e liquidação de fundos
item.description: Os contratos futuros de soja negociados na bolsa de Chicago caíram na quinta-feira devido à liquidação de fundos e às expectativas do mercado de que o processamento nos EUA em agosto provavelmente tenha diminuído, segundo operadores.
item.dc:creator: P.J. Huffstutter
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de soja negociados na bolsa de Chicago caíram na quinta-feira devido à liquidação de fundos e às expectativas do mercado de que o processamento nos EUA em agosto provavelmente tenha diminuído, segundo operadores. A pressão de oferta proveniente da colheita do que se espera ser uma safra recorde nos EUA também pesou sobre os preços da soja, juntamente com preocupações sobre a demanda de exportação, afirmaram analistas de mercado. Um final de verão e início de outono chuvosos nos EUA retardaram o ritmo da colheita, mas os novos suprimentos ainda pesam sobre os preços e estão desviando o foco dos operadores dos problemas de qualidade da safra relacionados ao clima, disse Jack Scoville, vice-presidente da Price Futures Group em Chicago. O trigo fechou em alta em um pregão volátil, já que uma safra reduzida nos EUA e uma grande licitação de importação anunciada pela Arábia Saudita ajudaram a impulsionar os preços. No início do pregão, o contrato do cereal mais negociado na bolsa atingiu US$6,70-3/4 por bushel, o menor preço desde 14 de agosto. Os futuros de milho encerraram o pregão em alta, impulsionados por uma onda de compras técnicas, depois que os operadores passaram grande parte do dia analisando um relatório surpreendente sobre os estoques dos EUA. Os agricultores e processadores de grãos dos EUA tinham 35% a mais de milho em estoque em 1º de setembro do que no ano anterior, informou o Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA na quarta-feira, um aumento maior do que o esperado. O contrato mais negociado de soja da CBOT fechou em baixa de 9 centavos, a US$12,84 por bushel. No início do pregão, o contrato chegou a cair para US$12,7375, o menor nível desde 28 de agosto. O milho encerrou com alta de 1,50 centavo, a US$ 5,0225 por bushel, após ter atingido anteriormente US$4,95 por bushel -- o preço mais baixo desde 19 de agosto. O trigo fechou com alta de 7 centavos, a US$6,8275 por bushel. A preocupação com a desaceleração do ritmo de processamento da soja nos EUA adicionou pressão aos futuros da soja durante o pregão, segundo os operadores. O USDA informou, após o fechamento do mercado, que os processadores de soja dos EUA processaram 209,6 milhões de bushels de soja em agosto, abaixo da média das estimativas do mercado.

item.title: Ibovespa fecha em alta com Petrobras; investidor aguarda eleição
item.description: O Ibovespa fechou em alta nesta quinta-feira, sustentada principalmente pelas ações da Petrobras , com o pregão já entrando em modo espera para o primeiro turno das eleições no Brasil.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa fechou em alta nesta quinta-feira, sustentada principalmente pelas ações da Petrobras (PETR3.SA) , com o pregão já entrando em modo espera para o primeiro turno das eleições no Brasil. Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) subiu 0,46%, a 187.197,46 pontos. Na máxima do dia, chegou a 187.436,73 pontos. Na mínima, recuou a 184.767,78 pontos. Pesquisas eleitorais têm mostrado uma disputa acirrada entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), elevando a probabilidade de que o pleito seja definido apenas no segundo turno, no final de outubro. De acordo com estrategistas, porém, o primeiro turno no próximo domingo pode servir como um termômetro, com investidores analisando a diferença entre as pesquisas e o resultado real do primeiro turno para inferir quem deve ser o próximo presidente. "Caso Lula tenha mais votos que os cerca de 40% indicados nas pesquisas, é bem provável que ele seja visto como o grande favorito", afirmou o estrategista-chefe da Eleven Research, Fernando Siqueira, em relatório nesta semana. "Caso Flávio tenha mais votos que os cerca de 37% a 38% das pesquisas, ele será visto como o grande favorito", acrescentou, avaliando que o pós-eleição deve trazer bastante volatilidade. Nova pesquisa Datafolha deve ocupar as atenções no começo da noite nesta quinta-feira, que ainda reserva debate entre os candidatos a presidente na TV Globo, embora sem a presença de Lula, que participará do podcast Flow. Estrategistas do BTG Pactual avaliam que, se Flávio vencer, as ações brasileiras poderiam voltar rapidamente à sua média histórica de 10 anos, o que implicaria um potencial de upside entre 11% e 20% em reais. "Se o Ibovespa subir até um desvio-padrão acima da média, o 'upside' poderia variar entre 32% e 45%", escreveram em relatório com recomendações de ações para outubro. Na visão da equipe do BTG, se Flávio for eleito, os participantes do mercado devem esperar medidas mais decisivas para enfrentar os desequilíbrios fiscais urgentes do país, o que deve desencadear um rali. Por outro lado, eles avaliam que a reeleição de Lula pode provocar alguma correção de mercado, com o Ibovespa recuando cerca de 10%, voltando aos 170 mil pontos. No exterior, o norte-americano S&P 500 (.SPX) fechou o primeiro pregão do mês com alta de 0,19% e o rendimento do título de 10 anos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos marcava 5,2365% no final da tarde, de 5,283% na véspera.

item.title: Asia’s Gasoline Margin Skyrockets on Outages, China Export Halt, Traders Say
item.description: By Mohi Narayan Asia’s gasoline margin rose to a record high on Thursday as various outages at regional refineries and reports that Chinese refiners have halted fuel exports for October tightened the supply outlook, traders said. The refining profit, or crack, GL92-SIN-CRK for gasoline rose to $50.53 per barrel over Brent crude. Chinese refiners …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
By Mohi Narayan

Asia’s gasoline margin rose to a record high on Thursday as various outages at regional refineries and reports that Chinese refiners have halted fuel exports for October tightened the supply outlook, traders said.

The refining profit, or crack, GL92-SIN-CRK for gasoline rose to $50.53 per barrel over Brent crude.

Chinese refiners have  suspended  oil product exports for October, four people briefed on the matter said, as Beijing looks to preserve domestic stocks, a move that will further crimp war-constrained fuel markets.

“Brent futures rolled onto next month’s contract yesterday, with an associated drop in crude price. This would have contributed to the widening crack, which also was supported by news of China reducing its product exports, so tightening the Asian market,” said Alan Gelder, senior vice president, refining, chemicals and oil markets at consultancy Wood Mackenzie.

The price for benchmark-grade fuel jumped to $150.69 per barrel, the highest level since March this year.

“Inventories are low and there are refinery outages too, pushing up prices,” a Singapore-based gasoline trader said.

India’s state-run Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd on Wednesday canceled three spot export tenders for refined fuels after a fire broke out at a processing unit.

“The export tender is expected to be refloated soon after evaluating the situation,” the refiner informed the exchanges on Thursday.

A key South Korean refiner also shut its gasoline-producing unit due to “some issue”, market sources said.

Singapore, China, India and South Korea are key gasoline exporters in Asia.

Meanwhile, Singapore’s light distillates stocks, including naphtha and gasoline, fell to a five-year  low  of 10.514 million barrels in the week to September 30, driven by a rise in transport fuel exports, data from Enterprise Singapore showed.

Gasoline imports totalled about 187,000 metric tons (approximately 1.6 million barrels) during the period, while exports climbed to roughly 672,000 tons.

Outbound gasoline volumes were led by Australia at about 189,000 tons, followed by Indonesia at 160,000 tons. Gasoline inflows were led by China at nearly 78,000 tons, followed by South Korea at about 46,000 tons.

item.title: Putin says the world is living through a dangerous moment, warns West not to escalate
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would resort to all weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear ones, if its territory of Kaliningrad were attacked.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Putin says the world is living through a dangerous moment, warns West not to escalate

Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would resort to all weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear ones, if its territory of Kaliningrad were attacked.

Russian President Vladimir Putin speaks at the session of the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow on Oct 1, 2026. (Photo: AP/Pavel Bednyakov)

FAST

MOSCOW: President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday (Oct 1) the world was living through a dangerous moment and warned the West not to escalate a standoff over Ukraine by threatening the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, which Moscow has made clear it would defend with nuclear weapons if necessary. Locked in a war in Ukraine, which he said Russia had no choice but to launch in order to safeguard its own security, Putin said Russia had no plans to attack any European country and wanted to coexist peacefully. But he reiterated that Moscow would resort to all weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear ones, if its most westerly territory - Kaliningrad, which is wedged between Poland and Lithuania - was threatened. "If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation - in this case, we are referring to Kaliningrad, and perhaps other territories as well - the question of the Russian Federation deploying all the weapons at our country’s disposal will, of course, inevitably and immediately be on the agenda," Putin told the Valdai Forum of international Russia experts in Moscow.

"This is inevitable," he said. Putin said Russia realised it would be facing "an enemy (NATO) twice our size". "And we will have to make use of our competitive advantages in this struggle. Yes, of course, France and Britain are nuclear powers - we understand that perfectly well and are fully aware of it," he said.  "But no one else possesses the kind of weapons that Russia has today. That is our competitive advantage."

Related:

Zelenskyy says Ukraine ready for maritime truce and puts onus on Russia to respond

Europeans warn of rising Russian sabotage but see no imminent NATO attack

NUCLEAR WARNING Putin's comments followed a diplomatic note which NATO said this week it had received from Russia, warning the Western military alliance it would be ready to resort to nuclear weapons if NATO attempted to cut off Russia's Baltic exclave. Russia's warning highlighted Moscow's urgent concern at what it has presented as a growing NATO threat to Kaliningrad, a heavily militarised Russian territory that is slightly bigger than the US state of Connecticut.  NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance had responded by emphasising that it was a defensive alliance and that nuclear threats were not helpful. Relations, already dire since Putin's decision to send troops into Ukraine in 2022, have worsened this year, with European governments accusing Moscow of stepping up a "hybrid war" on the continent through acts including sabotage and arson. Russia denies that, and rejects repeated statements by Western politicians that it is gearing up for a possible military attack on a NATO country. Putin warned that cycles of escalation in international conflict could quickly lead to dangerous scenarios. "We must realise that the moment when nothing can be changed any longer may come very quickly and unexpectedly for everyone. The logic of escalating, increasingly harsh retaliatory measures leads to a fatal point of no return," he said. "At the heart of this escalation lie arrogance and overconfidence. This is a path to the brink of the abyss. All the more so today, when the arsenals of the world’s leading powers contain weapons capable of destroying all life or, at the very least, reducing the Earth to a catastrophic state," Putin said. "Can we be certain that these weapons will never be used? Well, of course not. We must bear this in mind and avoid such an outcome," he added. Putin, who said he was ready for a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump if a proper agenda was worked out first, ruled out the idea of stopping Russian strikes on Ukrainian targets in the Black Sea area, while conceding that Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries across Russia had cost Russia 1 per cent of its gross domestic product. He said Russia was now responding to Ukraine in kind. But while he cast Western help to Kyiv when it came to launching deep strikes inside Russia as a future threat, he said Moscow was not planning to attack arms factories in Europe which supplied Ukraine "tomorrow".

Source: Reuters/fs/rl

item.title: ＥＵ、ディーゼル巡り米と協調姿勢 欧州の備蓄放出に「強い確信」と米エネ長官
item.description:
David Lawder
[ミルウォーキー １日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
David Lawder

[ミルウォーキー　１日　ロイター] - 欧州委員会のシェフチョビッチ委員（通商・経済安全保障担当）は１日、グリア米通商代表部（ＵＳＴＲ）代表とディーゼル燃料の供給逼迫や価格高騰について協議し、欧州が価格引き下げに向けた協調的な取り組みを望んでいると伝えた。

シェフチョビッチ氏は、２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）貿易相会合で記者団に対し、ディーゼルの輸出を制限するいかなる措置も想定外であり、欧州の経済活動に悪影響を及ぼすと述べた。

ロイターはこれに先立ち、トランプ米政権がドイツとフランスに対し、世界的な燃料価格高騰の緩和に向け緊急用ディーゼル備蓄の放出を求め、応じない場合はディーゼル輸出の禁止措置が講じられる可能性があると伝えたと報じていた。

シェフチョビッチ氏は、グリア氏とこの話題について詳細には踏み込まなかったとした上で、欧州は昨年スコットランドのターンベリーで結ばれた貿易合意に基づき、米国産エネルギーを購入するという約束を既に上回って履行していると指摘した。

さらに、ディーゼルを巡る協議については「予期せぬ事態を避けるため、緊密に連絡を取り合うことを明確に決定した」と説明。その上で「欧州側には、協調的なアプローチを取り、解決策を見い出すという意向と強い志向があることを理解している。何よりもまず、大西洋を挟む米欧市民への供給を確保することが重要だと考えている」と述べた。

こうした中、ライト米エネルギー長官は１日、米ＦＯＸニュースに対し、欧州が緊急用ディーゼル備蓄を取り崩すことで、世界的な燃料価格の高騰緩和に貢献できると「強く確信している」との考えを示した。

「欧州も状況の改善に貢献できるはずだし、そうしてくれると強く確信している。収穫期と、冬季の暖房油需要期を迎える今こそ、ディーゼル備蓄を協調して放出する時だ。今こそ市場により多くのディーゼル燃料を供給する時であり、その備蓄は既に存在している」とし、「近いうちに明るいニュースが届くと思う」と述べた。

item.title: Lawyer Tony Buzbee must face $25 million defamation lawsuit, judge says
item.description: Prominent Texas lawyer Tony Buzbee has failed for now to defeat a $25 million defamation lawsuit brought against him by a Mississippi attorney he accused of soliciting his former clients to bring lawsuits against him.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: Prominent Texas lawyer Tony Buzbee has failed for now to defeat a $25 million defamation lawsuit brought against him by a Mississippi attorney he accused of soliciting his former clients to bring lawsuits against him. US District Judge Vincent Brown in Galveston, Texas, ruled that Buzbee and his law firm must face the lawsuit from Marcy Croft, which grew out of litigation involving rapper Shawn "Jay-Z" Carter. The judge denied a motion to dismiss the case, ruling that the court at this early stage of the case could "reasonably infer" that Buzbee made defamatory statements about Croft, who has represented Carter's entertainment company Roc Nation. Buzbee said in an email that Croft's lawsuit is a "completely frivolous case and it will massively backfire on her." Gregg Costa, a lawyer at Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher representing Croft, said in a statement that they looked forward to "holding the defendants accountable for the reputational damage they caused to a distinguished and honorable lawyer." The ruling marks the latest development in a multi-front legal battle spanning nearly two years. At its core was a lawsuit brought by Buzbee against Carter in Manhattan federal court on behalf of an anonymous plaintiff who claimed she was drugged and raped by Carter and Sean "Diddy" Combs when she was 13 at an afterparty for the 2000 MTV Music Awards. Carter and Combs denied the allegations, which the plaintiff later withdrew. That lawsuit spawned other litigation from Carter against Buzbee in California state court, as well as a case Buzbee brought against Croft, Roc Nation and Carter's lawyers at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan in Texas, alleging that Croft used agents who solicited his former clients in order to bring claims against him. Both cases were dismissed. Croft's defamation lawsuit in Texas cites social media posts by Buzbee and says his claims of illegal client solicitation were part of a "coordinated campaign to falsely accuse a well-respected attorney of criminal conduct." The lawsuit seeks at least $25 million in damages. Carter has also sued Buzbee for defamation and malicious prosecution in New York federal court, after Buzbee's client [USN:L1N3P518Y TEXT:"dropped her lawsuit"] against the music stars last year. In that case, Carter claims Buzbee pursued rape allegations he knew to be false in the hopes of securing a payout. Buzbee, in court papers filed last month, countered that Carter was using the court system to harass both the alleged victim and her lawyers. Last week, Buzbee's former client [USN:L6N45H0YJ TEXT:"recanted her claim of rape"] against Carter and said she never met the billionaire rapper. She said she did not review the lawsuit against Carter before it was filed. Buzbee has asked a Manhattan federal judge to strike his former client's declaration . "Everything that is being said by Carter's team is a lie and it will be proven to be a lie with documents and audio, and even video," Buzbee told Reuters. Jordan Siev, a lawyer for Carter at Reed Smith, said in a statement they have their own evidence supporting the statement of Buzbee's former client that she had not met the rapper and had not reviewed the lawsuit. "We look forward to a full exposition in court," Siev said.

item.title: US judge finds law criminalizing noncitizen voting unconstitutional
item.description: A US judge dismissed a federal case on Thursday that accused a Jamaican national of illegally voting, finding the law criminalizing noncitizen voting was unconstitutional and delivering a blow to the Trump administration's campaign against alleged election fraud.
item.dc:creator: Tom Hals
item.content:encoded: A US judge dismissed a federal case on Thursday that accused a Jamaican national of illegally voting, finding the law criminalizing noncitizen voting was unconstitutional and delivering a blow to the Trump administration's campaign against alleged election fraud. The ruling by Miami-based US District Judge David Leibowitz applies only to the case of Florida resident Chelsea Cox, who was charged in October 2025 with illegally voting in the 2020 election. It is not binding for judges in other cases. It marks a setback for President Donald Trump's administration on noncitizen voting, a cornerstone of its push to highlight alleged election fraud ahead of November's midterm elections. Republicans are fighting to retain majorities in both houses of Congress. The Justice Department has charged at least 60 people with noncitizen voting since Trump returned to office in January 2025. The ruling by Leibowitz, who was nominated by Democratic President Joe Biden, appears to be the first time a federal court has found the 1996 law a violation of the US Constitution. Leibowitz wrote that under the US Constitution only states can set voter qualifications, not Congress. Every state requires US citizenship to vote, and Leibowitz said it was up to Florida, not the Department of Justice, to prosecute her for violating that requirement. "Can the State of Florida prohibit and punish the exact conduct Defendant Cox allegedly engaged in here? This has already been decided elsewhere and is not addressed here: Florida can and does," Leibowitz wrote. Trump, who falsely claims that fraud cost him the 2020 election, has said stricter enforcement of documented citizenship is needed for election integrity. His critics say the administration's highly publicized crackdown on noncitizen voting exaggerates a rare problem and could undermine confidence in election results. Neither the White House nor the Justice Department immediately responded to requests for comment. In a court filing, the Justice Department had said Congress, not the states, was best-equipped to handle immigration and foreign affairs. "Foreign interference in elections is clearly within the purview of Congress," federal prosecutors wrote. OTHER DEFENDANTS HAVE CHALLENGED LAW Cox's attorney Bruce Udolf welcomed the ruling. "This is a situation that cries out for discretion by government officials and they'd be well-advised to walk away from this without further reprisal against her," he said. Cox entered the United States as a tourist in 1999 and remained after her visa expired the next year, according to a court filing by the government. She used a fraudulent US Virgin Islands birth certificate to obtain a Florida driver's license and used those documents to register to vote in 2012. Records show she voted in federal elections from 2012 to 2020, but only the 2020 election was within the statute of limitations. There are about 45 pending noncitizen voting cases around the country and at least four other defendants have challenged the law on similar grounds. Judges in those cases may find Leibowitz's reasoning persuasive, but they are not bound by his decision. Trump has portrayed noncitizen voting as part of a broad Democratic Party conspiracy to dilute Republican power. But Cox was one of just 129 people charged with violating the law known as "voting by an alien," according to a Reuters investigation published in July. The investigation, published on July 19, found no defendant accused of conspiring to sway an election, backing a candidate or taking payment for a vote. The Reuters investigation also showed that most of the people accused of noncitizen voting were lawful permanent residents who either registered by mistake or were encouraged to sign up to vote based on the misguided advice of an election worker or government clerk. Illegal voting is grounds for deportation, and as Reuters has reported , the Trump administration has been investigating noncitizen voting and deporting defendants, sometimes years after their criminal cases were closed. Cox's attorney Udolf said he hoped the government would not move to deport her, citing her declining health. On July 16, Trump said without evidence that 278,000 noncitizens were registered to vote in California, Nevada, New Jersey and Pennsylvania. [USN:FWN40W0VO TEXT:"Five days later"], New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, a Democrat, said about 400 noncitizens in her state voted after a software error mistakenly registered about 6,600 people in 2023-24. [USN:L6N43O14O TEXT:"The Justice Department"] has demanded their names, nationalities and addresses.

item.title: Christa Pike gets "life-saving medical care" after surviving Tennessee execution
item.description: Christa Pike survived a failed execution attempt in Tennessee and is receiving “life-saving medical care” in hospital, according to her lawyers.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Christa Pike gets "life-saving medical care" after surviving Tennessee execution

Christa Pike survived a failed execution attempt in Tennessee and is receiving “life-saving medical care” in hospital, according to her lawyers.

This undated photo provided by the Tennessee Department of Correction shows Christa Pike. (Photo: AP/Tennessee Department of Correction)

WASHINGTON: C hrista Pike was receiving "life-saving medical care" in a Nashville hospital on Thursday (Oct 1) hours after she survived two attempts by Tennessee to execute her with lethal injections , her lawyers said , renewing scrutiny of capital punishment in the US. Pike , 50, was sentenced to death in the 1990s after a jury convicted her of a murder she carried out as a teenager. Her botched execution on Wednesday at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution, the second this year in Tennessee, highlights the difficulties US states face in carrying out lethal injections and in finding suitable alternative methods of capital punishment . "Christa is alive right now," Randall Spivey, one of Pike's lawyers, told reporters on Thursday afternoon. "We don't have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment, but we do know that she is alive right now and receiving life-saving medical care." Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, who denied Pike's clemency appeal to commute her sentence to life in prison on Monday, ordered a suspension of scheduled executions in Tennessee for the rest of the year and a third-party review of Wednesday's failed attempt.

"There is no one that wanted what happened last night to happen," Lee, a Republican, told reporters. "It's a tragedy, and it's deeply disturbing to me that that has happened in this state. The people deserve better and we're going to make sure that happens." Tennessee switched to a one-drug lethal injection protocol using pentobarbital, a powerful barbiturate, in 2024. Prison officials injected two syringes into Pike , her lawyers said in a late-night court filing, causing her "unnecessary agony" but not killing her.

Related:

US Supreme Court sides with Tennessee to allow its first execution of a woman in 200 years

Tennessee officials said the execution was halted, and she was taken away in an ambulance. Kayla Hackney, a Department of Correction spokesperson, declined to answer question's about Pike's condition on Thursday. Pike would have been the first woman executed by Tennessee in more than two centuries. Most countries in the world have abolished the death penalty, and the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said Pike 's case showed that the US should follow suit. "The prolonged suffering – physical and mental – arising from multiple failed execution attempts is abhorrent, and cruel," Turk said in a statement. Pike was 18 in January 1995 when she, her 17-year-old boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and a third companion lured Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old classmate at their Knoxville Job Corps vocational center, into a wooded area where they tortured and killed her. Pike and Shipp confessed to the killing, and both were convicted of first-degree murder.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Ireland and Austria draw 2-2 in game briefly halted by protesters
item.description: Ireland drew 2-2 with Austria in the Nations League on Thursday in a game disrupted after tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch at the Aviva Stadium by those protesting against the Irish team fulfilling their fixtures against Israel.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ireland drew 2-2 with Austria in the Nations League on Thursday in a game disrupted after tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch at the Aviva Stadium by those protesting against the Irish team fulfilling their fixtures against Israel. Ireland were 1-0 up in front of a sell-out crowd when the referee suspended the match briefly in the 20th minute as a small number of tennis balls featuring the Palestinian flag were thrown onto the pitch from behind both goals. The players were sent for a cooling break and play resumed just over two minutes later. A man draped in a Palestinian flag attempted to enter the pitch later in the first half, before being led away by security. Ireland are one of Europe's most outspoken critics of Israel's war in Gaza , and protests calling for the team to boycott the fixtures with Israel have been ongoing since February's Nations League draw pitted the two countries together. Ireland keeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad on the eve of Sunday's [USN:L6N45J074 TEXT:"3-0 away win"] over Israel, played in Hungary, which went ahead after the players held two votes on Saturday, with a majority opting to fulfil the fixture. The rest of the game passed away without further incident and the Stop the Game campaign issued a statement at halftime. "The protest is now over," the statement said. "It was a token act, deliberately limited, but necessary and done in solidarity with Gavin Bazunu and the people of Palestine facing genocide." PARROTT ON THE DOUBLE Troy Parrott put Ireland ahead in the 12th minute with a delightful goal, weaving and nutmegging his way past three Austrian defenders and into the area before striking low into the far corner. Parrott doubled Ireland's lead from the penalty spot on the stroke of halftime but the hosts let their two-goal lead slip after the break with substitutes Alexander Prass and Michael Gregoritsch netting for Austria. Bazunu was on the bench for Thursday's game but will not take part in the home game against Israel, scheduled for next Sunday, which was moved by the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) to Serbia and will be played behind closed doors in Backa Topola. FAI members [USN:L8N3WJ27T TEXT:"voted in November"] for its board to request that UEFA suspend Israel from European competitions, but a motion in favour of proceeding with the fixtures was passed at a meeting in July. During Ireland's friendly with Qatar in May at the Aviva Stadium, the match was halted twice during the first half, for a similar protest.

item.title: Boeing white-collar workers approve contract offer, averting strike fears
item.description: Boeing's largest white-collar union said on Thursday its members approved a sweetened contract offer, ending fears that a strike would stall work on two long-delayed jetliners and slow the pace of aircraft deliveries.
item.dc:creator: Shivansh Tiwary, Dan Catchpole
item.content:encoded: Boeing's (BA.N) largest white-collar union said on Thursday its members approved a sweetened contract offer, ending fears that a strike would stall work on two long-delayed jetliners and slow the pace of aircraft deliveries. The Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace, which represents about 17,000 Boeing workers, said both of its bargaining units voted to approve the new four-year offer. "We secured many victories that some thought were completely out of reach when this negotiation cycle started. All of these gains would not have been possible without your individual actions and our collective strength," the SPEEA negotiation team said in a public statement to members. Union members now "need to work with Boeing, and as needed, pressure Boeing management" to rebuild "trust with the membership that has eroded over the past decades" and "restore aerospace professionals and technicians to the center of Boeing's universe," the statement added. Boeing's 737 MAX crisis, which began with two fatal crashes in 2018 and 2019, revealed widespread safety and quality problems at the company that critics attributed to leadership's increasing focus on financial results in recent decades. The contract ratification provides relief for Boeing, easing concerns over a potential strike as early as October 7, the day after current contracts expire. “We're pleased with the outcome of the vote. We look forward to working with our team to support our company's continued recovery and meeting our customer commitments now and into the future," Ben Nimmergut, Boeing vice president and functional chief engineer for production engineering, said in a statement. A work stoppage could have delayed critical certification efforts for the 737 MAX 10 narrowbody and 777X widebody jets, while also disrupting the company's plans to increase production and accelerate deliveries. The contract [USN:L6N45317M TEXT:"proposal"] included a guaranteed 10% wage increase upon ratification, along with annual raises of 4% and the possibility of an additional 2% pay hike based on performance. About 68% of the professional unit, which represents roughly 13,000 engineers and scientists, voted in favor of the deal, as did more than 53% of the technical unit, representing about 4,000 designers, analysts and technicians. The two units bargain together but vote separately. Members of both the professional and technical units had previously [USN:L6N44I12F TEXT:"rejected"] Boeing's initial offer, which linked guaranteed raises to inflation, capped at 3%, with up to an additional 2.5% based on performance. SPEEA's last strike against Boeing was in 2000, when engineers and technical workers walked out for 40 days in a dispute over pay and benefits. The stoppage, which affected commercial aircraft production and deliveries, was one of the largest white-collar strikes in US history.

item.title: Global M&A deal rush fades in third quarter as rising borrowing costs bite
item.description: Global M&A activity in the third quarter totalled $993 billion, down 41% compared to the prior quarter, marking the first quarter to fall below $1 trillion since the second quarter of 2025, according to LSEG data.
item.dc:creator: Anousha Sakoui, Echo Wang
item.content:encoded: Global M&A activity in the third quarter totalled $993 billion, down 41% compared to the prior quarter, marking the first quarter to fall below $1 trillion since the second quarter of 2025, according to LSEG data. Banca Monte dei Paschi's [USN:L8N45607I TEXT:"$32 billion bid"] for Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) and Gold Fields' (GFIJ.J) $25.7 billion [USN:L1N45K003 TEXT:"bid"] for Northern Star Resources (NST.AX) were among the 10 deals over $10 billion announced in the third quarter, the lowest number of quarterly megadeals since the fourth quarter of 2024. While the boom in artificial intelligence and data centre building has lifted the outlook for economic growth, surging energy costs have been fanning inflation and pushing expectations higher about where interest rates will settle. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield hit [USN:L6N4570XY TEXT:"5.34"]% on Thursday, its highest level since 2002, after posting the biggest quarterly rise this century in the three months to September. "At the margins [higher yields] makes valuations sometimes a little tougher," said John Collins, global head of M&A at Morgan Stanley. "That said, the impact is hard to quantify, so I'm not ready to call a slowdown based on what we are seeing." So far this year worldwide M&A is up 28% to $3.9 trillion, the highest level in the period since 2001, while the number of deals fell 8%, levels not seen since 2020. “Corporates are still looking for scale or access to markets and technologies they are not in," said Carsten Woehrn, Goldman Sachs' co-head of M&A in Europe, Middle East and Africa. He sees total deal value exceeding the 2021 peak if the pace continues. "Megadeals are continuing and we’ve seen significant activity since the summer," Woehrn said. "Boards feel a greater urgency to pull the trigger on strategic deals.” Historic levels of investment in the technology sector have bolstered deals, with strategic stake purchases in those companies accounting for about one quarter of global M&A so far this year. Earlier this year, both Claude maker Anthropic and ChatGPT maker OpenAI raised tens of billions of dollars from investors. While US and European dealmaking fell sharply in the last three months, Asia Pacific M&A totalled $242 billion, up 8% from the second quarter and up 36% from the same period last year. This has been the strongest year to date for global private equity-backed dealmaking by value since records began in 1980, but the third quarter also saw a slowdown versus the same period last year. "We had an extraordinary Q2. Q3 is a normalization rather than an end of a cycle,” said Sarah Jones, global head of corporate at law firm Clifford Chance. “Strategics are still working to pursue their goals.” Cross-border dealmaking remains a strong theme this year to date, up 32% on the same period last year. "We're seeing a fair amount of appetite from US companies thinking about acquisitions in Europe for the first time, taking advantage of a strong dollar. In reverse, you're seeing people considering investment in the U.S. to take advantage of the potentially higher growth opportunity in the country," said Charlie Bouckaert, JPMorgan’s global head of M&A. TRILLION-DOLLAR IPOs AND DEALMAKING New listings, particularly in the technology sector, have fuelled M&A giving the companies new currency to buy up rivals. SpaceX (SPCX.O) [USN:L4N42O0VX TEXT:"acquired"] AI coding startup Cursor just days after its blockbuster Nasdaq debut, which saw its valuation surge to more than $2 trillion. "One of the drivers of activity is that being larger may help companies navigate transition in AI better," Collins said. The June IPO of Elon Musk's SpaceX helped drive $215 billion worth of initial public offerings, excluding SPACs, priced globally in the year to date, the highest level since 2021, from a lower number of deals than in the same period last year. In the last three months, stock sales raised $284 billion, 26% less than the proceeds raised across equity capital markets during the second quarter, though marking a 39% increase from the third quarter of 2025, thanks to offerings from SK Hynix (000660.KS) and Intel (INTC.O) . Some bankers did sound a note of caution that some investors were taking more of a pause when approaching some technology and AI-related deals. "Until about 10 days ago, no one seemed to worry about the midterms, but with rising diesel prices and rates and a risk of a change in political direction, it is prompting caution,” said Andreas Bernstorff, global head of equity capital markets at BNP Paribas. In recent weeks some IPOs have been delayed as higher interest rates and setbacks in the data centre ecosystem [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"threaten to derail"] a slew of new issues from the sector. But even with the uncertainty ahead, bankers remain confident. “Strong secular trends (such as AI) are driving activity, and we expect 2027 to be another robust year,” JPMorgan's Bouckaert said.

item.title: Canada is not close to restoring housing affordability, says central bank
item.description: By Promit Mukherjee
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: By Promit Mukherjee OTTAWA, Oct 1 (Reuters) - Canada is on the right track to addressing the issue of housing affordability but still has a way to go and needs more time, senior Bank of Canada deputy governor Carolyn Rogers said on Thursday. Restoring affordability will require more supply, better planning and infrastructure, regulations that protect resilience, and incentives that do not add demand to a market already short on supply, she told a business audience in Victoria, British Columbia. Here are the highlights of her speech: * As house prices go up they push rents higher as well as limit people's ability to buy, but at the same time if prices fall it shrinks the overall household wealth. "It feels a bit like a trap," she said. * The affordability goal has to be a mix of policy which could increase supply, protect resilience and reduce the economy's dependence on rising house prices. * "We're on the right track on many of these things, but we have a way to go and it will take time," she said. * Monetary policy can influence demand across the economy, including demand for housing, but it is too blunt a tool to deal with affordability issues * There are no simple fixes to the monetary policy framework that can help * The BoC needs to explain these trade-offs better and be clear with Canadians about what monetary policy can and cannot do, she said. (Reporting by Promit Mukherjee, editing by David Ljunggren) ((Reuters Ottawa editorial; david.ljunggren@tr.com )) Keywords: CANADA CENBANK/

item.title: 仏政府が27年緊縮予算案提出、540億ユーロ節減 財政懸念で国債利回り上昇
item.description:
Leigh Thomas
[パリ １日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Leigh Thomas

[パリ　１日　ロイター] - フランス政府は１日、財政赤字削減に向けて緊縮の色合いが濃い２０２７年度予算案を議会に提出した。大統領選を来年４─５月に控えて与野党は対立を深めており、審議の難航は必至だ。過去に複数の首相が辞任に追い込まれる中、ルコルニュ首相も難しい議会運営を迫られそうだ。赤字削減の実現に懐疑的な受け止めが投資家に広がり、１日の取引でフランスの１０年物国債利回りは一時４．９６％まで上昇した。

マクロン政権は、財政赤字の対国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比を今年度の５．４％から２７年度には５％に縮小させることを目指している。予算案は、公務員の賃金や年金支出の一部の凍結、地方予算や医療費の抑制、雇用主への税制優遇措置の縮小を盛り込んだ。レスキュール経済・財務相は記者団に「今回の予算案で、財政再建の軌道に戻る」と述べ、予算削減額は総額５４０億ユーロ相当で、うち４３０億ユーロが２７年度の新たな措置だと説明した。

一方、個人や企業を対象とする広範な増税には踏み込まなかった。

フランスでは、エネルギー価格の高騰や生活費の上昇に対する国民の不満が高まっている。９月２９日には公務員が賃金凍結に抗議してストライキを実施。教員不足や老朽化する施設の改善を訴える高校生のデモも拡大している。

フランス国立統計経済研究所（ＩＮＳＥＥ）は９月２９日、足元の政府債務残高は対ＧＤＰ比で１１９％に達し、第２次大戦後で最も高くなったと発表した。財政余力が少なくなる中、大統領選の有力候補と目されている極右政党、国民連合（ＲＮ）のマリーヌ・ルペン前党首や急進左派ジャンリュック・メランション氏の財政運営に対しても、市場は警戒感を示している。

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（1日）
item.description: ＜ロンドン株式市場＞ 下落して取引を終えた。銀行株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は４日続落し、約３カ月半ぶりの安値を付けた。...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（1日） 4:08 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞　下落して取引を終えた。銀行株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は４日続落し、約３カ月半ぶりの安値を付けた。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は１．６２％下落。原油高によるインフレ懸念と長期金利の上昇が相場の重荷となった。    英３０年債利回りは１９９８年以来となる一時５．９３５２％まで上昇。英１０年債利回りも一時５．４０３３％を付け、２００７年以来の高水準となった。    ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は４．２１％安。金融大手ＨＳＢＣは４．０％、バークレイズは４．１％、ナットウエストは５．４％いずれも下落した。    生活必需品株指数は１．５５％、製薬・バイオテクノロジー株指数は２．１１％それぞれ下落。    住宅建設株指数は４．８５％下落。金利上昇を受け、９月の英住宅価格は２５年１２月以来の低い伸びとなった。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞　３日続落して取引を終えた。銀行株が売られ、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種指数は約３カ月半ぶりの安値を付けた。長期金利の上昇が相場の重荷となった。地域別では、フランスのＣＡＣ４０指数は１．６２％安となり、下げが目立った。    フランス１０年債利回りが２００２年以来の高水準を付けた。    大半の業種が下落し、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種銀行株指数は３．７４％安。金融大手ＨＳＢＣは４．０％、バークレイズは４．１％、ナットウエストは５．４％いずれも下落した。    デンマークのバイオ企業シェラン・ファーマは６．１％安。    一方、テクノロジー株指数は０．４７％高。フランスのＩＴサービス大手キャップジェミニは７．４％上昇した。ドイツの９月の消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）の前年同月比の伸びは市場予想を上回った。ユーロ圏の８月の失業率は６．４％と、市場予想と同水準だった。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　域内国債利回りの動向が明確に二極化した。債務負担の重い加盟国の利回りが急上昇する一方、安全資産とされるドイツやオランダの国債利回りは低下した。債務拡大や高騰する原油価格、根強いインフレを背景に、投資家が安全性を求めていることを反映した形だ。    国債利回りは最近、世界的に上昇圧力にさらされており、前日にはユーロ圏の国債利回りが２０２２年以来となる四半期ベースで最大の上昇幅を記録した。    １日の取引は変動が激しく、国債利回りは当初全般的に急上昇した後、上げ幅を縮小。その後、フランスやイタリアの利回りが跳ね上がる一方、ドイツとオランダの利回りはこの日も低下したままとなった。    ドイツ２年債利回りは１４ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）近く低下して３．０５％、オランダ２年債利回りは約１２ｂｐ低下。    一方、イタリア２年債利回りは９ｂｐ超上昇して３．６３％、フランス２年債利回りは約７ｂｐ上昇して３．６９４％となった。    二極化の動きは１０年債利回りにも反映された。ドイツ１０年債利回りは約６ｂｐ低下して３．５２％、イタリア１０年債利回りは６ｂｐ超上昇して４．７０４％となった。    フランス国債は最近、特に強い売り圧力にさらされている。高水準の債務と２０２７年大統領選挙を控えた政治リスクの高まりが、政策金利の上昇見通しに重なっているためだ。フランス１０年債利回りは、やはり変動の激しい取引を経て、約７ｂｐ上昇して４．９３％となった。    独仏１０年債利回り格差＜DE１０FR１０=RR＞は約１４０ｂｐ。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、これは２０１２年５月以来の最大水準となった。

Oct 1 : SoftBank Group said on Thursday it has completed its $30 billion investment in OpenAI as part of its commitment to the ChatGPT maker's last fundraising round. Here are some other details: • Earlier this year, OpenAI had secured $122 billion in commitments that valued the Sam Altman-led company at $852 billion. Amazon, Nvidia and SoftBank had anchored the fundraising. • The Japanese investment conglomerate, led by founder Masayoshi Son, previously agreed to invest the capital through three tranches of $10 billion each through its Vision Fund 2.

• SoftBank raised $11.1 billion last month in the largest high-yield corporate bond sale globally to fund its mammoth bet on OpenAI. • It has become one of the world's biggest backers of OpenAI under founder Son's push to make the Japanese conglomerate a dominant investor in AI. • SoftBank's cumulative investment in OpenAI stands at $64.6 billion, giving it a 13 per cent stake in the AI lab. • It has canceled the remaining $10 billion of undrawn capacity under its $40 billion bridge loan secured earlier this year.

Source: Reuters
